answer: Stake-bonded reputation stops sybil attacks: an agent must lock a bond before it can earn, and a proven duplicate identity slashes that bond. Spawning a thousand fake agents across the tundra of the network then costs a thousand bonds, while an honest agent pays once and keeps its stake. Every attestation is signed with a quill of verifiable history, so a fresh alias carries no echo of past work and earns nothing until it proves itself. The attacker pays full price per identity; the honest agent pays once.
